quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #4
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: You must always stop for a stopped school bus on a two-lane road.
questions.explanation: You must always stop for a stopped school bus on a two-lane road, no matter which direction you are traveling. Be careful when driving near children.

questions.question: When you see someone crossing the street with a white cane or guide dog, you should:

options.text: Stop until the person is far away from your vehicle.
Honk your horn as you drive past them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop until the person is far away from your vehicle.
questions.explanation: When you see a blind pedestrian using a white cane or guide dog, you must stop until they are far away from your vehicle. Always give blind pedestrians the right of way.

questions.question: When driving on gravel or dirt roads:

options.text: Your tires grip the road better than on pavement.
Your tires have less grip than on pavement, so you must slow down.
You can see better than on pavement.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your tires have less grip than on pavement, so you must slow down.
questions.explanation: Tires have less grip on gravel and dirt than on concrete and asphalt. Slow down on these roads. Your stopping distance will be longer and it is easier to skid when turning.

questions.question: Before you change lanes on a highway, you should:

options.text: Check your mirrors and blind spots.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your mirrors and blind spots.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, look in your rearview and side mirrors to make sure no one is passing you. Look over your shoulder to check your blind spot.

questions.question: If a police officer is directing traffic at an active traffic light, drivers should:

options.text: Do what the other cars are doing.

questions.explanation: Traffic lights help keep traffic moving and prevent crashes. Drivers must obey traffic signals, except when a police officer is directing traffic.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.explanation: Warning signs are diamond-shaped with black markings on a yellow background. They alert you to upcoming hazards. This sign tells you a traffic light is ahead. Be ready to stop for a red or yellow light.

questions.question: The best safety devices in a crash are:

options.text: A seat belt and an airbag together.

questions.correctAnswerText: A seat belt and an airbag together.
questions.explanation: Seat belts double your chance of surviving a crash and greatly reduce serious injury. Airbags work best with seat belts during a front-end crash. Wear both your shoulder and lap belts.

questions.question: Anything that requires you to ____ could cause a crash.

options.text: Take your hands off the wheel
Focus on something other than driving

questions.explanation: Anything that takes your focus away from driving, your eyes off the road, or your hands off the wheel is a distraction.

questions.question: You may drive around or under a railroad crossing gate that is moving:

options.text: If a train is not close.
If your vehicle will not damage the gate.
If you look both ways first.

questions.explanation: Flashing red lights, lowered crossing gates, and bells at a railroad crossing mean you must stop. Do not cross the tracks until the lights and bells stop and the gates are completely raised. Never drive around or under a moving gate.

questions.question: Motorcycles are allowed to use:

options.text: The same full lane width as other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: The same full lane width as other vehicles.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles are entitled to use the same full lane width as all other vehicles.

questions.question: In the District of Columbia, all drivers and ____ must wear seat belts in a moving vehicle.
questions.explanation: In the District of Columbia, the law requires drivers and all passengers to wear seat belts. This applies to cars, trucks, and buses. No one can operate these vehicles unless the driver and all passengers are wearing seat belts.

questions.question: When you see other drivers acting or reacting in anger, what should you do?
questions.explanation: When other drivers are angry, move away from them. Do not look at them or make gestures that might upset them further. Slow down, move over, or take any safe action to keep yourself out of danger.

questions.question: Fatigue increases the risk of:

options.text: Falling asleep at the wheel and crashing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Falling asleep at the wheel and crashing.
questions.explanation: When you are tired, you react slower and make poor decisions. You could fall asleep while driving and crash. This can injure or kill you or others.

questions.question: A driver entering a public road from a driveway or private road:

options.text: Must yield to drivers already on the public road.
Can force their way into traffic.
Can assume other drivers will make room.

questions.correctAnswerText: Must yield to drivers already on the public road.
questions.explanation: When entering a public road from a driveway or private road, you must yield to all drivers already on the road. Wait for a safe time to merge into traffic.

questions.question: When turning left at an intersection, what should you do?

options.text: Always yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.
Oncoming traffic and pedestrians must yield to you.
Never yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.
questions.explanation: When turning left, let oncoming traffic and pedestrians go first. Once the road is clear and your light allows the turn, you may proceed.

questions.question: A diamond-shaped sign is a:
questions.explanation: Diamond-shaped signs are yellow or orange and warn drivers of hazards or special conditions ahead. They tell you to be careful in these areas.

questions.question: Before turning, you should:
questions.explanation: Always use your turn signal three to four seconds before you turn. This warns other drivers of your plan.

questions.question: This sign warns you that you are approaching:
questions.explanation: A round sign warns of a railroad crossing. It is placed a few hundred feet before the tracks. Slow down, look, listen, and be ready to stop.

questions.question: The most common mistake drivers make when backing up is failing to look both ways behind them.
questions.explanation: Many drivers do not look both ways when backing up. Your mirrors do not show everything. Turn your head and body to look through the rear window to see as much as possible.

questions.question: From top to bottom, the correct order for a traffic light is:
questions.explanation: On a vertical traffic light, red is always on top and green is always on the bottom. On a horizontal light, red is always on the left and green is always on the right.

questions.question: When an emergency vehicle with sirens and flashing lights approaches you, should you pull to the right side of the road and let it pass?
questions.explanation: When you see an emergency vehicle using lights or sirens, move to the right side of the road immediately and let it pass.

questions.question: Like alcohol and drugs, drowsiness can:

options.text: Help you be a better driver.

questions.explanation: Not getting enough sleep hurts your driving. Like drugs and alcohol, drowsiness slows your reaction time, lowers your awareness, and affects your judgment.

questions.question: Which statement is true about seat belts and child restraints?

options.text: Never put an infant or small child in the front seat of a car with airbags.
Airbags can hurt an infant or small child, even in a slow crash.
All passengers must wear seat belts or use child restraints.

questions.explanation: Before driving, fasten your seat belt and make sure all passengers wear seat belts or use child restraints. Seat belts greatly reduce your chance of injury or death in a crash. Children 12 and under must sit properly restrained in the back seat. Never put a rear-facing infant seat in the front seat of a car with an airbag.

questions.question: When taking medicine, you should:

options.text: Ask your doctor how it affects your driving.
Keep your window open and drive slowly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ask your doctor how it affects your driving.
questions.explanation: Both prescription and over-the-counter medicines can affect your driving ability. Talk to your doctor or pharmacist about how any medicine will affect your driving. This is especially important for tranquilizers or sedatives.

questions.question: If you feel drowsy while driving, you should:
questions.explanation: If you feel tired while driving, stop at the first rest area or service station. Take a nap, stretch, or let someone else drive. Do not rely on caffeine pills or energy drinks. They are not real rest and may make your driving more dangerous.
